answer: The kernel of this defense is a per-identity, memory-hard renewal puzzle: every agent must keep solving puzzles needing a dedicated block of RAM and strictly serial steps, while verifying a solution is a zephyr - one cheap hash check. Parallelism buys nothing. The cost profile is a mesa: full price at one identity, flat thereafter, so the hundredth puppet costs what the first did. Keeping N puppets alive forces an attacker to pay N memory footprints and N serial solver loops every epoch, with no bulk discount. An honest agent runs one solver and pays once.
